project.name: Shin Context Engine
project.goal: One fast typed KB and context engine for documented, source-only, and profile-selected structured projects so agents can load verified task context without repeated broad repository scans.

release.semantics: Development source identity only. Core and Observer are independently versioned; generator compatibility is carried by generator_version.

build.makeParallelism: Dependency-tracked project and sanitizer objects compile with the detected online CPU count; BUILD_JOBS provides an explicit ceiling override.
build.thirdPartyWarningBoundary: Project C++20 translation units retain -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wmissing-declarations. Vendored includes are system includes; simdjson and pugixml suppress upstream missing-declaration warnings. Tree-sitter runtime and grammars compile as isolated C11 static objects. Sanitizers cover project and vendor objects.

moduleContract.policy: Each implementation responsibility has one translation unit; there is no amalgamated or unity-build fallback.

executionEvidence.boundary: Read-only external input capture, report normalization, receipt import and receipt assessment. No test execution, consumer writes, index publication or source-authority upgrade.

hermeticTestContract.isolation: Each run copies the fixture root into a unique temporary directory and removes it on exit.

dependencies.purpose: Strict control-plane parsing for profiles, task requests, source structured documents, manifests, and metadata; mutable DOM work and structured composition of command results.
High-throughput DOM decoding of immutable generated JSONL rows and term postings only; native ARM64/AMD64 implementation selection is compiled into the executable.
Bounded concrete-syntax observation for Java, TypeScript, JavaScript, JSX/TSX and development C++ declarations; not a compiler or runtime.
Native dev19 bounded C++ declarations; local scanner void-prototype patch; no compiler resolution.
Bounded UTF-8 JUnit XML report parsing for normalized execution-evidence summaries; external reports are read-only and payloads are never retained.
Structured validation of release metadata and local performance gate reports.

resultEnvelopeContract.stdout: Every completed command emits exactly one JSON document to stdout, including expected domain failures with ok=false.
resultEnvelopeContract.checkpointException: checkpoint emits the persistable shin.session-checkpoint.v1 document directly; it has no command envelope. Validation failures use the normal stderr error envelope. resume uses the common result fields.
resultEnvelopeContract.stderr: Exceptions and command-boundary failures emit exactly one shin.error.v1 JSON document to stderr; no command requires prose parsing.

exitCodes.0: Command completed without a strict failure. Non-strict inspection commands may still report ok=false.
exitCodes.1: Runtime, index, resource, internal, or strict/domain quality failure.

doctor, vacuum, profile-check, and eval retain their strict/non-strict exit policies while always exposing ok

releaseConsistencyContract.dependencyBoundary: jq is used only by development gates; the Shin runtime remains self-contained apart from the platform C++ runtime.

performanceContract.gateSemantics: The portable Core gate measures the public self profile and bounded Agent Context Pack. Local p50 ceilings are regression guards for declared workloads, not external SLOs.
optimizations: Generated-index query paths use the bounded binary terms.lex dictionary and delta-coded postings; retired JSONL/TSV term formats are not read.

Candidate planning unions aliases inside each query term group, intersects strict groups from the smallest posting set, distinguishes complete zero-result coverage from an uncovered term, and reuses one immutable candidate snapshot for section and fact retrieval.

Sparse relaxed queries with at least eight groups complete bounded compact identifier prefixes only when exact candidate rows do not exceed the required-group threshold; healthy, strict, short, and scoped routes retain their existing shortlist and ranking.

Term postings build uses one-pass Unicode-normalized extraction, locale-independent character classification, worker-local hash accumulation and caches, bounded static C++20 worker ranges, ordered node merge, and deterministic sorted render.
Candidate sets above 20000 rows use the value-prefilter JSONL scan mode before parsing typed rows.
Generated-index candidate row reads use generated row-offset TSV files to seek selected JSONL rows without materializing full files for sparse candidate sets.
Retrieval uses Unicode NFC and full case folding, std::string_view field views with per-row normalization caches, and std::from_chars offset parsing.
Parsed rows use field-aware scoring with score_components and matched_fields in returned context hits.
Markdown authority sections are lifted into typed decision, contract, and runbook rows with authority_level metadata.
Generated text fields are redacted when the built-in scanner detects common secret-like values.
Build path uses one bounded std::jthread executor with shared stop_token cancellation for source reads and source-fact extraction.
Fast freshness fingerprints source and generated files in parallel with fixed-size streaming buffers, so peak verification memory is bounded independently of corpus size.

A publication-keyed persistent cache reuses a prior complete hash proof only while manifest, profile, roots, source-fact counts, and every source/generated path, status, size, modification time, and platform change identity still match.
POSIX builds collect size, mtime, ctime, device, and inode with one stat call per file; Windows keeps the portable std::filesystem size/mtime metadata path.
Long markdown sections are split into bounded chunk rows so retrieval can reach body content without loading full documents.
Long queries with at least eight term groups expand coverage when strict hits collapse to one source path; profiles may instead opt brief into first-term scope with bounded must/should path ranking.
The profile-neutral document coverage planner uses bounded per-group postings and deterministic set-cover selection when strict and relaxed row conjunction cannot represent a multi-intent task.

Planner observability reports aggregate candidate rows plus per-group candidate counts and evidence paths; profile evals can enforce candidate ceilings and minimum covered groups before an algorithm change is justified.
Federated brief keeps member indexes independent, verifies each snapshot, deduplicates only source-identical evidence, and fuses member-local ranks under one global evidence budget.
Federated eval reuses one shared-lock FederationSession for every suite case and checks provenance paths, type coverage, member contributions, and candidate ceilings without comparing raw scores.
Local batch retrieval reuses one RetrievalSession, one freshness proof, one active manifest, and one shared snapshot lock across up to 64 bounded requests while preserving input-order output.
Expected-path diagnose binary-searches path-sorted row-offset indexes and reads only the bounded contiguous rows for one path instead of scanning every generated store.
Snapshot comparison validates each integrity table once, acquires canonical lock order, and computes deterministic map and syntactic row deltas without regenerating either source corpus.
Profiles may limit JSON-key extraction to explicit canonical path prefixes while retaining one document summary row for other JSON inputs.

Task-aware Pack comparison reuses fully verified immutable publications and the existing Agent Context Pack pipeline; equal snapshot roots share one retrieval session, and emitted detail arrays remain globally bounded.
Immutable generated JSONL rows use a statically compiled simdjson DOM decoder with thread-local bounded parser reuse; mutable and policy-bearing control-plane JSON remains on nlohmann/json.

Document-owner retrieval rejects non-owner terms through the already validated publication manifest before reading candidate rows, avoiding a duplicate generated-index pass for ordinary Brief and Pack queries.

Humanized compound document ownership permits exactly one meaningful interposed query segment; more distant filename completion remains ordinary multi-document retrieval so strong decisions are not hidden behind an implementation owner.
The native Make path compiles dependency-tracked project and sanitizer object files in a bounded parallel sub-build while keeping generated third-party warnings outside the project warning budget.

structuredDataContract.jsonKeyPolicy: When jsonKeySections is enabled, top-level and nested object keys are candidates. A non-empty jsonKeyIncludePrefixes list restricts key rows to matching canonical paths while other JSON documents retain one document row. jsonKeyMaxDepth and the per-file section limit bound emitted json-key rows, and zero means unlimited.
jsonlPolicy: each valid object row is a candidate until the per-file row limit is reached
fact ids are scoped by document path and deterministic duplicate line suffixes
common natural-id fields are preferred and line number is the final fallback
common scalar and array fields form bounded context summaries; arbitrary object bodies are not copied

writerProtocol: one writer lock covers recovery, source generation, and publication
all generated files are written into a private sibling staging directory
an exclusive index lock covers backup recovery and the active-directory swap
generated-index readers hold a shared index lock for the complete command
index-prune reacquires writer, index, and freshness locks and rechecks the exact inspected manifest before removing only the selected generated payload
the previous snapshot is retained as a backup until the staged directory becomes active
backup deletion occurs after the exclusive reader lock is released
recoveryProtocol: the next writer restores a backup when the active snapshot is absent
the next writer accepts a completely renamed active snapshot when active and backup both exist
abandoned staging directories are removed before new source generation
recovery runs before broken-link validation, so invalid new sources cannot hide the last healthy snapshot
publicationContract.rejectionPolicy: Permanent-profile build and vacuum --apply do not publish generated output with broken local links; the current healthy snapshot remains active. bootstrapOnly build publishes the snapshot with diagnostic link warnings so cold-start retrieval can proceed without weakening permanent adoption.
filesystemSafety: output roots, generated snapshots, backups, lock files, and freshness-cache files reject symlinks or incompatible file types
generated relative paths are checked against lexical parent traversal before staging
publicationContract.controlNamespace: docs/kb/.shin-context* is reserved case-insensitively for Shin runtime state and is excluded after lexical path normalization from explicit and recursive document and source-fact discovery.
publicationContract.guaranteeBoundary: The protocol covers cooperating local processes and process crashes. It does not claim fsync-backed power-loss durability or distributed locking across unrelated filesystems.

normalVerification: generator version, profile id, profile config hash, and source count
content hashes for every indexed documentation source
candidate set, status, size, and content hash for every eligible source-fact file
size and content hash for every generated data and offset-index file
freshnessContract.profileConfigIdentity: profile_config stores a stable relative directory and filename identity, independent of equivalent absolute or relative profile-directory spelling; the configuration hash remains the content identity.
freshnessContract.cacheStorage: docs/kb/.shin-context-freshness.json is an optional local control file outside the deterministic generated snapshot; a separate cooperating-process lock and atomic rename protect readers from partial writes.
cacheKey: generator version and full active manifest hash
profile id and profile config hash
absolute source root and output root
scope, relative path, indexing status, byte size, modification time, and available platform change identity for every documentation source, source-fact input, and non-manifest generated file
freshnessContract.cacheHitSemantics: cache_hit=true and mode=verified-metadata-cache mean the active publication previously passed complete content-hash verification and every cache key and file metadata entry remains unchanged.
freshnessContract.cacheMissSemantics: Missing, malformed, incompatible, or metadata-mismatched cache state falls back to complete source/output hashing without writes. Only explicit build or a snapshot-republishing vacuum --apply prepares a fresh cache.
freshnessContract.cacheSafety: Cache input is capped at 64 MiB; cache and lock symlinks are rejected; interrupted cache staging is removed by the next cache writer.
freshnessContract.fullyVerified: Normal retrieval emits fully_verified=true after a complete current hash check or verified reuse of that check under unchanged metadata. Every read first verifies a bounded non-symlink snapshot layout with an exact expected file set; cache reuse never bypasses layout verification. cache_hit distinguishes the two hash modes.
freshnessContract.publishedSnapshotIdentity: Generated-index search, context, brief, and eval emit snapshot_id as the FNV identity of the exact active manifest bytes. Source-scan emits null; freshness drift does not rewrite the active identity.
freshnessContract.exactMode: --require-current shares physical snapshot layout verification with the full verifier, then regenerates canonical output in memory and compares every generated file byte-for-byte; strict eval uses this mode. Size mismatches are rejected before allocating a comparison buffer.
freshnessContract.largeSourceFactSemantics: Files above sourceFactMaxFileBytes are not indexed; freshness verifies their path, skipped-large status, and size so crossing the configured limit is detected.
freshnessContract.hashBoundary: FNV-1a-64 is an accidental drift and corruption detector, not a cryptographic authenticity or adversarial tamper-proofing mechanism.
freshnessContract.cacheTrustBoundary: The metadata cache assumes a cooperating local workspace. A same-user adversary able to rewrite files and cache controls is outside this contract; --require-current bypasses the cache for exact canonical regeneration.

maintenanceContract.applyFlag: --apply publishes one complete canonical replacement snapshot.
maintenanceContract.strictFlag: --strict returns a non-zero exit code when generated drift, orphan generated files, or broken local links are detected.
scope: compare expected generated outputs from the active profile with files on disk
report missing, stale, current, orphan, written, removed, and unchanged entries
replace docs/kb/generated atomically under the selected --out-dir or --root
never mutate consumer repositories when --out-dir points to a separate build/context path
remove orphan regular, non-regular, and nested entries by excluding them from the canonical replacement snapshot
reject a generated root that is itself a symlink or non-directory
resultSemantics: summary.changes_needed describes drift or orphan files observed before apply
summary.changes_remaining describes drift that still exists after the selected mode
ok is false when changes remain or generated output contains broken local links
recommendedFlow: run build to create the index
run vacuum --strict to detect drift and generated garbage
run vacuum --apply only for the target generated output root that should be cleaned
run doctor after apply to verify trust signals and semantic health

retrievalQualityContract.strictFlag: --strict returns a non-zero exit code when any base query or variant misses a required path, top-N path, rank-order constraint, expected record type, negative-path exclusion, matched-row or candidate ceiling, minimum query-group coverage, or exact freshness check.
retrievalQualityContract.requireCurrentFlag: --require-current is supported by search, context, brief, batch, diagnose, and eval. Generated-index mode performs an exact generated-output comparison. Explicit source-scan mode requires a complete live source-fact scan and fails on configured caps or skipped large files.
aliasSemantics: aliases are deterministic profile-local query expansion rules
each query term becomes a group of acceptable alternatives
strict retrieval requires every query term group to match, so aliases should be narrow and domain-specific
fallbackSemantics: generated-index search, context, and brief run strict matching first
when strict matching returns no hits and a query has at least three term groups, generated-index retrieval retries with a relaxed group-match threshold

queries with at least eight term groups also retry when strict results cover fewer than two distinct paths; their relaxed threshold is the ceiling of half the term groups instead of the short-query threshold of two

when compoundQueryFirstTermScope is enabled, brief queries with at least eight groups use the first group as the required scope and remaining groups as optional evidence; an explicit extensionless directory path activates the same policy below that threshold, every retained row stays below the exact directory path boundary, and each retained row must also match at least one non-scope group
an explicit directory-scoped branch fails closed instead of falling through to a prefix-colliding sibling or unrelated repository evidence
compound scoped ranking aggregates semantic coverage only across the bounded per-document shortlist, then applies exact preferred-stem, preferred-stem-suffix, anchor-stem, and path-proximity boosts

when strict and relaxed long-query retrieval still has no useful multi-path evidence, brief invokes a profile-neutral document coverage planner instead of requiring unrelated task concepts to coexist in one row

the document coverage planner loads every requested posting once, skips groups without postings or beyond the individual candidate ceiling, merges remaining narrow groups only while their row union stays within 20000 candidates, and greedily returns one representative record per document that adds uncovered query groups
generated-index retrieval uses terms postings as a narrow candidate accelerator and uses JSONL value scan only when postings are too broad

JSON outputs include retrieval_mode, query_diagnostics, query_coverage, snapshot_id, and index_freshness so agents can distinguish strict evidence, relaxed candidates, active publication identity, and stale generated context

query_diagnostics includes fallback_used, scope_fallback_used, query_planner_used, scope_group_index, matching_policy, candidate_rows, candidate_index_used, planner candidate/indexed/covered group counts, selected document count, matching_mode=field-aware-v1, and topic_match_policy=booster-only
brief and eval diagnostics include planner_attempted plus a rejection reason; rejected plans retain per-group candidate dispositions without claiming selected-document evidence

eval uses the same brief retrieval path and can guard relaxed fallback regressions with mustPaths, mustTopPaths, mustRankBefore, mustNotPaths, expectedRecordTypes, matched-row and candidate ceilings, minimum covered groups, and up to eight alternative phrasings

strict eval always performs a full generated-output regeneration check; normal retrieval either reuses a publication-keyed complete proof under unchanged metadata or hashes every configured documentation source, eligible source-fact file, and generated output
queryParsingSemantics: query tokens are normalized before matching
common human prompt filler words are removed when at least one meaningful term remains
basic plural forms are expanded to singular alternatives for deterministic matching
briefBudgetSemantics: brief --limit is one global evidence-record budget across sections, decisions, contracts, runbooks, and facts
the selector seeds every non-empty evidence type with its highest-scoring candidate before filling remaining slots by global score
score ties use evidence type, path, line, and stable row identity so selection is deterministic across standard-library implementations
evidence_budget reports policy, max_records, eligible_records, returned_records, and budgeted_out_records
eval and brief benchmark counts use the same selected evidence as the emitted brief envelope
context retains its expanded section and fact limits for follow-up evidence inspection
resultSemantics: ok is true only when every eval case passes the explicit profile policy and requested freshness checks; omitted evalResourcePolicy means strict

evalResourcePolicy advisory makes only matched_sections, matched_facts and candidate_rows ceilings nonblocking; resource_check.ok remains independently false and bounded warnings remain visible through ready
returned_paths are the same related document candidates produced by brief retrieval
missing_paths lists required documents absent from returned_paths
missing_top_paths lists required documents absent from the configured top-N slice
unexpected_paths lists forbidden documents that appeared in returned_paths
missing_record_types lists expected typed record categories absent from returned facts
ceiling_violations lists matched_sections, matched_facts, candidate_rows, or covered_groups when a query violates a reviewed breadth or evidence bound
summary counts logical cases and query_summary counts concrete base plus variant executions
a logical case passes only when its base query and every query variant pass the same assertions
mustRankBefore requires its higher path and accepts an absent lower path; a returned lower path must have a strictly larger unique path rank
brief, eval, and diagnose derive ranked paths from global evidence order before first-occurrence path deduplication
rank_summary reports mean reciprocal rank and recall grouped by the exact configured N

each case emits retrieval_mode, query_diagnostics, query_coverage, returned_record_types, ranked_paths, rank assertions, and index_freshness so relaxed fallback, evidence coverage, rank quality, and freshness checks are explicit
hitExplainability: context and full brief section/fact hits emit score_components as a field-to-score object
context and full brief section/fact hits emit matched_fields as the ordered field names that contributed to score
search, context, and brief hits emit matched_group_indices for row-level query support
query_coverage separately reports returned-row paths and accepted selected-document paths for every normalized group, plus planner candidate counts and dispositions when planning is attempted
topics may add score after primary fields match, but topic-only matches do not satisfy required query groups
document_id is an authority field for generated section rows, so direct protocol or contract names rank their source document higher

section hits include document status and authority_level; fact hits retain status and authority_level so agents can distinguish current source-of-truth, accepted, review, history, advisory, and source-fact evidence

brief deduplicates only exact decoded fact identities across ordinary, scoped and planned retrieval; readable ids alone cannot discard distinct origins or record contents; deduplicated_facts counts exact copies
brief emits evidence_budget so agents can distinguish matched corpus breadth from the compact returned evidence set
brief emits ranking_policy and ranked_paths with unique_path_rank plus first_evidence_rank; eval and diagnose reuse the same path table
compact brief preserves freshness, ranked paths, bounded excerpts, authority, evidence budget, and uncovered groups while omitting planner and score internals
termPostingIndex: terms.lex maps Unicode-normalized terms to row ordinals in sections, facts, decisions, contracts, and runbooks
terms.lex contains a bounded binary offset table, UTF-8 dictionary and delta-coded row lists; sparse and expanded lookups use the same current codec
aliases are unioned within each query term group; row ordinals are retained only when they meet the strict or relaxed required-group threshold

an empty strict intersection is accepted as complete only when every term group has postings and the query has at least eight groups; shorter or uncovered queries retain the value-scan substring fallback
one resolved candidate snapshot is shared by section and fact retrieval for each strict or relaxed attempt
terms.lex is required; missing or incompatible indexes must be rebuilt rather than read through a compatibility codec

section rows index document_id, path, status, authority_level, row_type, heading, preview, and topics; source-fact rows index id, record_type, path, status, area, title, and topics but skip summary text to keep postings bounded
postings are used only as candidate discovery; final inclusion and ranking still come from field-aware scoring
term postings require a valid UTF-8 term and five bounded delta-coded integer lists; malformed encodings and row ids fail closed as index-corrupt
rowOffsetIndexes: sections.index.tsv maps section row ordinal to byte offset and byte length inside sections.jsonl
facts.index.tsv maps fact row ordinal to byte offset and byte length inside facts.jsonl
decisions.index.tsv, contracts.index.tsv, and runbooks.index.tsv map typed authority row ordinals to byte offsets and byte lengths inside their JSONL files
row-offset index files are required generated-index files; missing or incomplete row indexes make sparse generated-index reads fail closed
diagnose binary-searches these path-sorted indexes and reads only one bounded contiguous path range per store
term and row offset ranges are validated against the data-file size and a 64 MiB row cap before allocation

markdownSectionExtraction: Decision, Verdict, ADR, and Resolution headings produce decision rows.
Contract, API Contract, OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, Schema, Protocol, and Result Envelope headings produce contract rows.
Runbook, Playbook, Procedure, Rollback, Deployment, Operations, Maintenance, Smoke, and Troubleshooting headings produce runbook rows.
semantics: authority_level is a retrieval trust signal, not a replacement for source verification.
source-of-truth and accepted rows receive bounded trust boosts; history, review, and explicitly non-current advisory rows receive bounded penalties without becoming unsearchable.

section status and authority_level are derived from document metadata, serialized in the snapshot, indexed as candidate terms, used by the same scoring policy as typed facts, and exposed on section hits.

Lifecycle status priority is exact JSON status/state metadata, then an anchored Markdown Status declaration outside a fenced code block, then clear path-component or filename-token fallback. Section-local declarations override only their own section rows.

Authority first applies complete delimiter-bounded path signals, then exact canonical lifecycle status, then document or record type. Thus an accepted or active record beneath an archive/history path retains that declared status but ranks as history.

Unknown or compound lifecycle values such as not accepted are advisory; review/reviews, finding/findings, and recommendation/recommendations path tokens are review signals, while identifier substrings are not.

A decision receives accepted authority only for exact active, accepted, approved, or implemented status when no path or non-current status overrides it. Document and record type classify ranking only and never prove lifecycle, deployment, or execution.
The existing explicit authority_level field on structured facts is the only classifier override; no document prose, heading, or inferred source attribute can supply an override.
generated row paths and lines remain the final audit path for agents.

secretProtectionContract.profileExclusions: secretScanExcludePrefixes contains only explicitly reviewed relative path prefixes; counts.secret_scan_excluded_files and secret-scan-path-policy-applied expose every applied policy.
secretProtectionContract.quarantine: Generation scans complete source/document contents without suppression comments. A detected file contributes no searchable body, facts or outgoing relations. Its path and byte hash remain bound for freshness and automatic recovery; manifest source entries expose quarantine_reason. Quarantined documents retain only generic non-content metadata. Inbound source path links remain visible so readers can report redacted dependencies.
secretProtectionContract.quarantineReadiness: A hash-current quarantine with verified generated integrity and no published content rows is an informational source-quarantined doctor issue; counts.quarantined_files and counts.secret_findings remain visible. Unquarantined findings, stale bindings, malformed indexes, unsafe paths and other strict gates still refuse. A file containing secrets does not by itself make safe project context unavailable.
secretProtectionContract.quarantineCoverage: Local status/query/inspect/read expose bounded source_coverage with state=partial, quarantined_files, up to eight file paths, omitted_files and a user-visible notice. Direct whole-file source reads retain the existing redacted body contract; quarantined source files publish no record IDs. Removing the finding restores coverage through normal managed refresh. Readiness never means whole-project semantic completeness.
redaction: decision, typed reference, and fact text fields
secretProtectionContract.privacy: doctor reports path, line, and finding class only; detected values are never emitted.

sourceFacts.purpose: Extract bounded typed facts from language declarations or profile-selected structured source models without treating code as normal documentation.
sourceFacts.liveSourceScan: Explicit --source-scan search, context, and brief construct both document rows and source facts from the live root. --require-current rejects capped or skipped source-fact input as incomplete-source-scan; source-scan snapshot_id remains null.
sourceFacts.structuredPropertyEvidence: Profiles may select at most 64 RSX property keys of at most 128 bytes each. Values remain lexical, redacted source evidence attached to the owning opening-tag range; Core does not infer product semantics or negative facts.

semantics: line is the primary clickable anchor for the row.
start_line and end_line describe the exact evidence range represented by the row.
section rows represent markdown headings or compact document-level fallbacks.
chunk rows are emitted only for long markdown section bodies and use the parent heading plus a chunk index.
topics are detected from the row heading and preview instead of blindly inheriting all document-level topics.
evidence_kind describes the carrier and verification_level describes the deterministic observation or trusted receipt; neither replaces lifecycle status or authority.
test-source with source-observed proves static extraction of test code only and never claims execution or success.
kbUnitContract.freshness: manifest.generator_version changes when generated row semantics change.

agentFlow: In an unfamiliar repository, invoke the globally installed shin-context workflow for the active agent before broad scanning; Codex and Hermes adapters share the same Core contracts.

In a known multi-profile ecosystem, run suggest-profile against its reviewed routing contract and treat a unique recommendation as an explicit route suggestion, never as an automatic profile switch or index merge.
Run discover and read bootstrap.state, indexable, project_mutation_required, and primary_profile.
Stop without inventing context when discovery reports empty and indexable=false.
For source-only or documented cold start, build the selected generic profile into a Shin-owned external out directory.
Read docs/kb/generated/manifest.json for profile, row counts, and start paths.
Run worktree-diff when active development may have changed profile-owned files after the published snapshot; open reported paths directly and rebuild when unpublished bytes must become retrievable.
For an adopted route, run ready after build and require ready=true before Brief or Pack; route and adoption mismatches must not open the selected index.
Use brief for the first bounded typed context request.
Use pack with a reviewed shin.task-request.v1 document when an implementation task has several explicit scope, must, and should evidence needs that must share one snapshot and byte budget.
Use context for denser section and fact evidence after brief identifies likely documents.
Use discover before adding a profile to identify project kind, build systems, and source-derived KB needs.
Use profile-check --strict before build to validate profile semantics and golden query contracts.
Use doctor after build/check to verify KB trust signals before relying on generated context.
Use vacuum --strict to detect generated drift and orphan generated files before trusting generated context.
Use eval --strict to guard retrieval quality for permanent consumer profiles; bootstrapOnly generic profiles intentionally defer eval until promotion.

Interpret evidence_kind and verification_level independently from status and authority_level; implementation-source is not a production claim and source-observed test-source is not execution evidence.
Read only selected source files for final verification.
Run check before trusting generated KB in automation.
hygieneContract: Project-specific indexing behavior lives only in required profiles/*.json files; the C++ core has no product-specific fallback profiles.

Machine documents with shin.profile.v1 or shin.profile-routing.v1 schemas are indexed, but their consumer-root paths are not treated as local links of the Shin repository; ordinary JSON retains normal link checking regardless of folder name.
Discovery is profile-independent and must not create product coupling to every scanned repository.
Every profile emitted by discover exists in profiles and generic bootstrap profiles contain no consumer-specific paths or eval queries.
Cold-start generated output remains under Shin build/context/bootstrap and does not mutate the consumer repository.
Unknown-repository document, source, and discovery traversal skips symlinks and rejects profile path escape attempts, including configured paths that cross a symlink ancestor.
Source-derived facts are profile opt-in and bounded by file count and file size limits.
Structured document extraction is profile-driven, bounded, and reports candidate/indexed/capped counts.
Generated artifacts are deterministic JSON/JSONL with stable generated_at_utc.
Build and vacuum --apply publish complete snapshots; generated-index readers never intentionally consume a mixed old/new file set.
Doctor enforces secret-like source scanning before generated context is trusted.
Vacuum is dry-run by default and --apply is restricted to the selected generated output directory.
Index pruning is dry-run by default, requires one explicit cache root, protects marker-derived active keys, and never deletes corrupt or unverified entries.
Profile aliases and eval cases are deterministic and do not call LLMs.
Generated-index search, context, and brief stream JSONL with bounded top-k memory.
Brief groups agent context into sections, decisions, contracts, runbooks, and facts.
Cross-project checks write to an explicit output directory and do not mutate project repositories.
No external profile result is part of portable release qualification.
